entries.title: Luke 8:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Mary Magdalene - Or Mary of Magdala, a town in Galilee: probably the person mentioned in the last chapter.

entries.title: Luke 8:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Who - keep it - Not like the highway side: And bring forth fruit - Not like the thorny ground: With perseverance - Not like the stony.

entries.title: Luke 8:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: No man having lighted a candle - As if ho had said, And let your good fruit appear openly. Mt 5:15; Mr 4:21; Lu 11:33.

entries.title: Luke 8:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For nothing is hid - Strive not to conceal it at all; for you can conceal nothing long. Mt 10:26; Mr 4:22; Lu 12:2.

entries.title: Luke 8:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The word commonly translated seemeth, wherever it occurs, does not weaken, but greatly strengthens the sense. Mt 13:12; Mr 4:25; Lu 19:26.

entries.title: Luke 8:29
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For many times it had caught him - Therefore our compassionate Lord made the more haste to cast him out.

entries.title: Luke 8:31
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The abyss - That is, the bottomless pit.

entries.title: Luke 8:32
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: To enter into the swine - Not that they were any easier in the swine than out of them. Had it been so, they would not so soon have dislodged themselves, by destroying the herd.

entries.title: Luke 8:52
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: She is not dead but sleepeth - Her soul is not separated finally from the body; and this short separation is rather to be called sleep than death.
